name: Seated cable row and chest-supported row
angleNote: Pull: 0% = arms straight (reaching to the pulley, or hanging), 100% = hands at the trunk. The trunk angle is held by the variant. Shoulder and elbow torques per arm, hip per side; drag the figure to turn it.

strength.note: Shoulder extension (positive) and flexion (negative) peak torque per arm, taken as constant across the range: Mayer's isometric means for men (93 and 68 Nm), measured standing.
strength.source: Mayer F, Horstmann T, Röcker K, Heitkamp HC, Dickhuth HH (1994). Int J Sports Med 15:S19–S25, Table 2 (men, dominant side, isometric)

strength.note: Horizontal abduction (positive: rear delts, with the elbows flared) and adduction (negative) per arm, taken as constant. No horizontal-abduction strength curve has been checked: Mayer's isometric shoulder abduction peak for men (47 Nm) is used as a stand-in, and the adduction peak is the bench's estimate.
strength.source: TODO: no horizontal-abduction source checked; stand-in from Mayer F, Horstmann T, Röcker K, Heitkamp HC, Dickhuth HH (1994). Int J Sports Med 15:S19–S25, Table 2 (men, dominant side, isometric)

strength.note: Shoulder external (positive) and internal (negative) rotation peak torque per arm, taken as constant: Mayer's isometric means for men (30 and 43 Nm).
strength.source: Mayer F, Horstmann T, Röcker K, Heitkamp HC, Dickhuth HH (1994). Int J Sports Med 15:S19–S25, Table 2 (men, dominant side, isometric)

strength.note: Relative isometric elbow-flexion torque vs elbow flexion (0° = straight), peak about 95°: the paper's mean cubic fit, normalised, inside the measured 32–120° (held flat beyond). Measured with the upper arm raised 90° and horizontally adducted 20°, not hanging as in a standing curl. Peak per arm: the paper's male means (flexion 85 Nm, extension 77 Nm).
strength.source: Pinter IJ, Bobbert MF, van Soest AJ, Smeets JBJ (2010). Isometric torque–angle relationships of the elbow flexors and extensors in the transverse plane. J Electromyogr Kinesiol 20:923–931. doi:10.1016/j.jelekin.2010.05.001

strength.note: No muscle capacity: the elbow's sideways moment is carried mostly by ligaments and the joint surfaces, so it is shown as torque only.
strength.source: Not applicable: carried by ligaments and joint surfaces, so no muscle strength is used

strength.note: Relative isometric hip-extension torque vs hip flexion, peak about 53°, measured standing with the knee slightly bent (tested −29° to 74°; deeper hip flexion is held flat at the 74° value, which is extrapolation). Relative curve = cos(C2·(θ − C3)) with the 18–25-year-old male means of Table 3; points only inside the tested range, so the app holds the end values flat beyond it. Peak torque default from the same table's C1 (young men, scaled to 73 kg and 1.75 m).
strength.source: Anderson DE, Madigan ML, Nussbaum MA (2007). Maximum voluntary joint torque as a function of joint angle and angular velocity: model development and application to the lower limb. J Biomech 40(14):3105–3113. doi:10.1016/j.jbiomech.2007.03.022

muscles.name: Latissimus dorsi
muscles.note: Main shoulder extensor: pulls the upper arm back towards the hips.

muscles.name: Posterior deltoid
muscles.note: Horizontal abductor: pulls the upper arm out and back when the elbows flare. With the elbows tucked the lats do that job instead.

muscles.name: Biceps, brachialis, brachioradialis
muscles.note: Elbow flexors: work while the forearm is tilted away from the line of the load.

muscles.name: Rhomboids, middle trapezius
muscles.note: Pull the shoulder blades together at the top. Not estimated: the model has no shoulder blade.

muscles.name: Erector spinae
muscles.note: Hold the trunk still against the cable's pull (and its own weight when leaning). Approximation: driven by the hip's effort; zero when a pad carries the chest.

muscles.name: Hamstrings
muscles.note: With the glutes, hold the hip angle against the cable pulling the trunk forward.

muscles.name: Infraspinatus, teres minor
muscles.note: External rotators of the rotator cuff: hold the upper arm from turning inwards.

muscles.name: Subscapularis
muscles.note: Internal rotator of the rotator cuff: holds the upper arm from turning outwards.

variants.name: Seated cable row, trunk upright
variants.notes: Trunk held upright, handle pulled to the belly. The cable pulls the trunk forward, so the hips and lower back hold it, most at the start, when the hands are far out in front and high above the hips. Close-grip (V) handle: the hands sit near the middle, so the cables pull the arms slightly inwards. The hands move in a straight line; elbows tucked in the side view's plane. Stack weight only: the machine's pulley friction is ignored.

variants.name: Leaning back 15°
variants.notes: Trunk leaning back: the body's weight behind the hips now counters the cable, so the hips and lower back do less. Leaning back during the pull (body English) uses this to shift work away from the arms. Close-grip (V) handle: the hands sit near the middle, so the cables pull the arms slightly inwards. The hands move in a straight line; elbows tucked in the side view's plane. Stack weight only: the machine's pulley friction is ignored.

variants.name: Leaning forward 20°
variants.notes: Trunk leaning towards the stack: both the trunk's weight and the cable now pull forward, so the hips and lower back work hardest. The lats pull through a longer arc. Close-grip (V) handle: the hands sit near the middle, so the cables pull the arms slightly inwards. The hands move in a straight line; elbows tucked in the side view's plane. Stack weight only: the machine's pulley friction is ignored.

variants.name: Chest-supported dumbbell row
variants.notes: Chest on an incline pad, trunk 50° from vertical, dumbbells hanging. The pad carries the trunk, so the lower back is out of it: the arms and upper back do all the work. Load = both dumbbells together. The hands move in a straight line; elbows tucked in the side view's plane.

variants.name: Wide bar, elbows out
variants.equipment: Cable, long bar, seat and foot plate
variants.notes: Long bar held wide, elbows flared about 70°, pulled to the lower chest: the rear delts and upper back do much more of the work, the lats and biceps less. Stack weight only; pulley friction ignored.

phases.name: Reach
phases.text: Arms long: the cable (or the dumbbells) pulls on straight arms; the trunk holds the load.

phases.name: Pull
phases.text: Elbows bend and travel back: the elbow flexors and lats share the work.

phases.name: Squeeze
phases.text: Hands at the trunk, elbows behind it: the lats do most of the work, and the shoulder blades squeeze together.
